pr.title: Plan launching Claude Code and Codex sessions from the console
pr.head: a9fb19ab6d0e3b226ff60a00682eaba818cbed8b

summary: Projector’s planned terminal console lets you answer and discuss work across live agent sessions. This draft extends it with a form that starts a Claude Code or Codex session in a chosen checkout, so each session does not need its own terminal window.

The console launches each host through its command-line interface, tracks startup in a local record, and opens a session’s chat on demand. This pull request adds only the plan; it implements no launcher.

The plan remains draft with priority next. Approval prompts, matching Claude Code background IDs, and attaching Codex to a daemon-held thread remain explicit open questions. They do not assert implementation readiness.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: One proposed command needs correction: a prompt beginning with a host option is parsed as that option. The required gate, exact-head CI, and project metadata checks pass.

groups.title: Start sessions and open their chats
groups.kicker: A draft design for launching from the console home list
intro: The New session form selects a host and checkout, accepts a name and prompt, and starts the host without a shell. A launch record lets the console show starting or failed before the session joins the live list.

The Chat key attaches through claude attach or codex resume. Inside tmux it opens a pane; elsewhere it temporarily hands the console’s terminal to the host. Fake executable tests check arguments and startup behavior, while real host approval and attachment behavior stays unresolved.

files.note: Adds the launch form, command arguments, startup record, chat attachment, acceptance cases, and unresolved host questions.

checks.text: Section 2.1 appends the prompt directly to Codex options. With the literal prompt --help, the installed CLI prints usage and exits 0 without a thread.started event. Put -- before the prompt and cover a leading-hyphen prompt in the acceptance tests.

Section 6 keeps approval prompts, Claude Code background-ID matching, and Codex attachment open. Projector reports this nested project as draft/next, so these questions make no executable-readiness claim.

Section 7 records a prior real Codex launch and wake test. This review checks that report against the current delivery adapter and installed CLI help; it does not start another background agent or repeat that historical test.
